claim: fixed-rho first-order rigid implies rational squared weights
evidence: Rigidity is NUMERICAL, inherited from cascade.jsonl. The weight field is EXACT, recomputed from the closed form rather than read off the integer-versus-string encoding.
scope_warning: 154 of the 799 shipped records are not natural-orbital representatives (results/data/attainer_gate_audit.json): their 1-RDM is not diagonal, so they attain the spectrum in another basis. Both the rigidity and the weight datum are properties of the shipped representative, so on those records the implication is a statement about that representative and not about the vertex. gate_passing_records_only is the subset where the statement is about a natural-orbital representative.
direction_check: Deformability does not force irrationality: the deformable class is overwhelmingly rational too, so the implication is one-way evidence and not a biconditional.

power_warning.finding: Every one of the 645 natural-orbital representatives is fixed-rho rigid, and all 59 deformable records are among the 154 that fail the gate.
power_warning.consequence: The implication's discriminating power lives ENTIRELY in the records that are not natural-orbital representatives. On the 645 gate-passing records the antecedent is always true, so the implication is confirmed there without any rigid-versus-deformable contrast to confirm it against. Quoting 740 of 740 as evidence for a statement about vertices overstates it in the same way the bracket holdout's 38 rows did: the count is right and the independent content is smaller.
power_warning.mechanism: Expected rather than surprising. The fixed-rho fiber fixes rho itself, and a record whose rho is not diag(lambda) is constrained differently from one whose rho is, so the two populations are not comparable observations of one law.
